title: A meet-once matching and the number of live junctions
claim: Decide whether every pointwise-live renaming preserving the full table of a reached meet-once stage extends to its successor. Bound how many live junctions a failure needs.
standard_statement: In a simple graph on ordinary parity sites with one external vertex, can a permutation of distinctions that preserves minimum common bond sizes and fixes every live star fail after the simultaneous splitting of the external vertex?
prior_work: The six-start GROWN-END-SWAP requires ordinary pairs meeting twice. The EXTEND-ROUND theorem preserves full equation-space matchings. The earlier census establishes its own finite population only.
source_contribution: An original five-distinction construction in a four-junction part, and a two-terminal replacement argument for the small-live case. Exact minimum sizes require separate complete finite checks.

validation.status: V1 internal. Distinct complete-round engines, exact connected-shore and XOR checks on the seven-start, independent literal lower-tier enumeration. Separate referee review pending.

completion_gate: Explicitly show two true rounds, all current entries, and failure on an old pair, or disposition of the proof obligation.
conclusion: The permutation exchanging AC and BC fixes every current pair distance and the growing end pointwise and changes an old successor entry from two to three in the specified meet-once histories.
evidence_class: Finite mathematical counterexample, size-independent structural lemmas, computer-assisted exact minimum on positive-age stages.
